# Proposal: Fractional AI Governance Advisor

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments
**Program:** AI Governance Academy, Fractional AI Governance Advisor
**Term and price:** 12 months, renewable, at US$10,000 per month
**Basis:** Discovery call notes of 6 October 2026

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It has about 1,100 staff and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Client has one AI system deployed: a customer service chatbot on the support portal. A second, AI visual inspection, is in pilot on the German production line. A third, AI sales forecasting, is planned for next year. The Client describes its AI maturity as Piloting. This is the Client's first Academy program, so there are no prior open items to carry forward.

Three facts shape this engagement:

- **Inventory finding.** An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded that the Client has no inventory of AI systems.
- **Production objective.** Your stated objective is to have governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027.
- **Certification target.** The Client intends to begin ISO/IEC 42001 work next year. The start date is not yet fixed and is recorded here as `Unknown`.

The Client names the EU AI Act and GDPR as regulatory drivers. It also names ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 9001 as incumbent frameworks. The extent to which existing records, processes or controls under those frameworks can support AI governance is `Unknown` and will be confirmed at intake.

Three stated constraints apply throughout:

- Customer data must stay in the EU.
- The German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff.
- Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.

## 2. The Case for Continuous Fractional Advisory at Piloting Maturity

At Piloting maturity, the Client's three use cases sit at different points in their lifecycle. One is live, one is moving toward production and one is still in planning. Governance decisions made for the visual inspection pilot will set the pattern that later use cases follow. A single project engagement could close the inventory finding. It would not, however, provide judgment at each later step: the production decision, the start of ISO/IEC 42001 preparation and the arrival of sales forecasting.

Fractional advisory keeps senior governance support available across that sequence without adding headcount. The engagement is guided by three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human. In practice, this means:

- Adoption is paced to the Client's capacity to govern it.
- Each AI use rests on a documented and understood purpose.
- Accountability for outcomes stays with named people at the Client.

## 3. Annual Arc

The arc is set out in engagement quarters. The engagement start date is `Unknown`. If the engagement begins shortly after the 15 December 2026 decision, Quarter 1 falls before the Q2 2027 production target. If the start date moves, the arc will be re-sequenced so that production governance work stays ahead of that target.

**Quarter 1: Stabilize.**
- Build the AI system inventory in response to the June 2026 finding, using the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook).
- Define AI governance roles and decision rights. Named owners are `Unknown` and will be assigned by the Client.
- Scope a risk and impact assessment for the visual inspection pilot.
- Map where AI-related customer data flows, against the EU data residency constraint.
- Help the Client plan the timing of works council consultation so that it precedes any production change.
- Prepare questions for external counsel to verify. These include how the EU AI Act applies to visual inspection and to the chatbot, and which GDPR obligations attach to each use case.

**Quarter 2: Deepen.**
- Design a pre-production governance gate for visual inspection. The gate will cover human oversight, acceptance criteria, monitoring and rollback.
- Record the completion of works council consultation as a gate condition.
- Bring the deployed chatbot under the same governance model.
- Apply paced adoption practices from the Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen).

**Quarter 3: Assure.**
- Begin ISO/IEC 42001 readiness work, including a gap assessment and an evidence collection plan.
- Coordinate the evidence plan with the Client's internal auditors.
- Audit preparation intensity peaks here by default. It will shift earlier or later once the ISO/IEC 42001 start date, currently `Unknown`, is fixed at intake.

**Quarter 4: Evolve.**
- Review ISO/IEC 42001 readiness and the maturity of governance artifacts.
- Run governance intake for AI sales forecasting ahead of its planned use next year.
- Structure executive and board reporting using AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).
- Prepare the Month 11 renewal options.

## 4. Cadence and Access Model

The baseline cadence has four elements:

- A monthly executive advisory session.
- A monthly working session with the governance team.
- Asynchronous availability for defined question categories.
- A quarterly governance review.

The audience roles named for this engagement are the General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and two internal auditors. Attendance at each session is `Unknown` and will be confirmed by the Sponsor at intake. Question categories, response windows and escalation paths will be agreed in the first month.

## 5. Scope

**In scope:** governance evolution, implementation guidance, audit preparation, AI strategy and executive decision support.

**Out of scope:** legal advice, certification body functions, staff augmentation and incident command.

The advisor is not counsel of record. Legal questions, including EU AI Act and GDPR interpretation, route to external counsel. Regulatory developments raised during the engagement are flagged for counsel verification and are not presented as settled advice. All certification work is framed as readiness, and no certification or audit outcome is promised.

## 6. Price

The price is US$10,000 per month over a 12-month renewable term, a total of US$120,000 for the term.

The stated approved budget is up to US$80,000 this fiscal year. The Client's fiscal year dates are `Unknown`, so it is not yet known how the twelve monthly fees fall across fiscal years. This should be confirmed before the 15 December 2026 decision. Price and duration are fixed program terms.
